rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes varying the Ti/heavy-transition-metal ratio in a single-phase HEA, while the paper added Tb to a specific V-Nb-Ti-Hf matrix, creating a different composition change and introducing secondary phases.
rationale.condition_agreement: Both involve cryogenic superconducting characterization, but the hypothesis specifies identical processing to avoid phase segregation, whereas the paper's as-cast alloys contained precipitates and were measured under specific fields up to 5–6 T.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes electron–phonon coupling modulated by local lattice distortions from Ti/heavy-metal balance; the paper attributes degradation to nonsuperconducting Tb/Tb2O3 inclusions, with no clear role for lattice distortions or Ti/heavy-metal ratio.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts enhanced Tc with more heavy transition metals; the paper found that adding Tb (a heavy lanthanide) lowered Tc and degraded superconductivity, opposite in direction.
